title: Five different answers can hide inside “Was LinkedIn worth it?”
author: Mykhailo Amplieiev
voice_status: Identity and role verified; one indexed excerpt is insufficient for stable voice calibration. Founder voice review remains pending; profile collection stayed stopped.
performer: Fictional presenter only. Do not resemble or impersonate either founder or any client.
theme: Five distinct value hypotheses, shown as separate measures rather than a funnel.
spoken_script:
If you ask whether LinkedIn was worth the effort, first say what kind of value you mean.

Did the founder spend less time? Do relevant buyers know what the company builds? Does a buyer arrive with a specific reason to trust the team? Are suitable conversations happening? Is a post being used in a real sales discussion?

Those are five separate hypotheses. They are not stages that everyone moves through, and a reaction count cannot answer all five. Choose the most important one for the engagement, agree on a baseline, and decide what evidence would count.

For time, include interviews and review. For conversations, separate a relevant discussion from a demo. For sales use, record the specific context. Which hypothesis would you measure first?
